name: Luxembourg
summary: Since 2023 adults may grow 4 cannabis plants per household and use it at home; ≤3 g in public is a €25–500 fine (usually a €145 ticket). Using other drugs: 8 days–6 months prison and/or €251–2,500.
callingForHelp: No specific Good Samaritan protection found; emergency medical staff are bound by professional secrecy.
drugChecking: Occasional drug checking (DUCK) offered by the PIPAPO party project (4motion asbl); no permanent public service found.

loi1973.title: Law of 19 Feb 1973 on medicines and drug addiction (consolidated 21 Jul 2023)

rgdStup.title: Grand-ducal regulation of 26 Mar 1974: list of narcotics (consolidated 12 Dec 2025)

rgdPsy.title: Grand-ducal regulation of 20 Mar 1974: psychotropic substances (consolidated 13 Jul 2026)

rgdT34.title: Grand-ducal regulation of 6 Feb 1997: Schedule III/IV psychotropics (consolidated 12 Dec 2025)

alc2006.title: Law of 22 Dec 2006 banning alcohol sales to under-16s

pipapo.title: PIPAPO (4motion asbl): party work and DUCK drug checking

lsd.note: Listed psychotrope. Using or possessing for own use: 8 days–6 months prison and/or €251–2,500; higher if in front of minors.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin is listed, and the list also covers organisms naturally containing it with established abuse potential, so magic mushrooms/truffles are covered.

dmt.note: DMT is a listed psychotrope; ayahuasca is therefore illegal.

mescaline.note: Mescaline is listed, and organisms naturally containing it (e.g. peyote) are covered; ornamental cactus sales may be tolerated.

dox.note: DOB, DOC, DOET and DOM are listed psychotropes. No generic analogue ban, so newer analogues may be unlisted.

nbomes.note: 25I-, 25B- and 25C-NBOMe are listed. No generic analogue ban: other NBOMes may be unscheduled.

2c-x.note: 2C-I and other 2C-x are listed (2C-B is internationally controlled). No generic analogue ban, so some newer analogues may be unlisted.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT and 5-MeO-MiPT were not found on Luxembourg's lists and there is no generic tryptamine ban; they appear unscheduled.

cannabis.note: Adults: up to 4 home-grown plants per household, use and possession at home legal. Public: ≤3 g = €25–500 fine (€145 ticket); more is a crime.

ketamine.note: Not on the narcotics/psychotropic lists checked; a prescription-only (mainly hospital) medicine.

dxm.note: Not a controlled drug (only levomethorphan is listed). Whether DXM cough medicines need a prescription was not verified.

nitrous.note: Not a controlled substance and no national law on recreational sale found (2026).

amphetamines.note: Amphetamines are internationally controlled; possession for own use: 8 days–6 months and/or €251–2,500. ADHD drugs on prescription.

mdma.note: Listed psychotrope. Own use: 8 days–6 months prison and/or €251–2,500 fine; supply much heavier.

cocaine.note: Listed narcotic. Own use: 8 days–6 months prison and/or €251–2,500 fine; supply much heavier.

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely.

alcohol.note: Selling or offering alcohol to under-16s is banned; no separate national age limit for spirits found.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is a listed psychotrope (sodium oxybate on prescription). GBL and 1,4-BD were not found on the lists.

opioids.note: Heroin banned (except an authorised heroin-assisted pilot); morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl are listed narcotics on prescription only.

tramadol.note: Not on the narcotics lists checked; prescription-only medicine.

maois.note: Prescription-only medicines. Harmala alkaloids are not listed, but ayahuasca contains DMT (listed).
